items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: It was always Teddy Wilson, Roy Eldridge, and myself.

ctx.x: They kind of looked out for eachother. So my not having any money really didn't make any difference. You know, when I went to New York, because I knew I didn't have anything to worry about. Like Freddy Green. When he would come to Chicago, Count would always tell me, John, come to New York. I said, Freddy, you know, I don't know anybody. He said, look, don't worry, you just come, we'll look out for you. You know. You can't get musicians to do that now. You know, they feel a little differently.

But I went to New York, as I said, and it was like going home. I never worried. I knew I was going to eat, I knew I was going play, and I had a place to sleep, you know, and that was it. So I -- how I started to recording with Mildred, I went to the Golden Gate Ballroom one night to hear Teddy Wilson's band, his new band. He had a marvelous band, and Mildred Bailey was there. And she saw me and was reunion. And I recorded -- I did all of her recording after that. It was always Teddy Wilson, Roy Eldridge, and…
I don't know. Well, any way, Pat, it's a mean, old world.
